disorder-name.detail: Schizophrenia spectrum disorder; two subgroups combined under the same Minor Category: SSD-V (n=38, with violence history: schizophrenia n=35, schizoaffective disorder n=1, schizophreniform disorder n=1, other psychosis n=1) and SSD-NV (n=138, without violence history: schizophrenia n=87, schizoaffective disorder n=17, schizophreniform disorder n=7, other psychosis n=27); all DSM-IV diagnoses. Violence comorbidity distinguishes subgroups within the study but both map to the same SSD Minor Category.
disorder-name.supporting_text: "persons with a history of severe violence and comorbid schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD-V; n = 38; i.e. schizophrenia n = 35, schizoaffective disorder n = 1, schizophreniform disorder n = 1, other psychosis n = 1)" ... "persons with no history of violence but with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD-NV n = 138; i.e. schizophrenia n = 87, schizoaffective disorder n = 17, schizophreniform disorder n = 7, other psychosis n = 27)"

dataset-of-origin.detail: SSD-V (forensic patients sentenced to compulsory mental health care) recruited from sTOP (Forensic Psychiatry study); SSD-NV (hospital wards and out-patient clinics, inclusion criteria age 12–65) recruited from TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis) and uTOP (Youth-TOP study, for participants aged 12–18 given SSD-NV min age=15.1). STROKEMRI contributed to healthy controls only.
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "Participants (n = 782 male/608 female) were recruited from the Oslo area as part of four studies: the Thematically Organized Psychosis study (TOP) [30], the STROKEMRI study [31], The Youth-TOP study (uTOP) [32], and The Forensic Psychiatry study (sTOP) [33]."

age.detail: Combined SSD-V (n=38, mean=34.7, SD=8.9, range 19.2–54.1) and SSD-NV (n=138, mean=29.0, SD=8.7, range 15.1–57.8); total n=176. Weighted mean=(38×34.7+138×29.0)/176=30.23 years (weighted); pooled SD=sqrt((37×8.9²+137×8.7²)/174)=sqrt(76.44)=8.74 years (pooled). Overall min=15.1 and max=57.8 taken from SSD-NV which had the wider age range.

sex.detail: All SSD participants (SSD-V n=38 + SSD-NV n=138 = combined n=176) were male. The paper explicitly states all individuals in the four groups were male due to the scarcity of eligible women in forensic psychiatry units and prisons.
sex.supporting_text: "All individuals were male due to the scarcity of eligible women within the participating forensic psychiatry units and prisons."
